event: Nala crosses to the apron and circles the pinned body wide, well clear of the fangs.
It reeks of river mud and scorched flesh; flies are already settling on it.
She spins up a water disc and sets it to the thick neck; in about a minute it shears through.
The head rolls free on the stone, heavy as a sack of meal, fangs a hand long.
Jory and both barge crews come picking down the bank to the apron, and the miller unbars his door.
Nala cuts into the belly beside the spikes, working toward the liver for twenty minutes.
The green sac lies whole beneath it. She ties off the duct with Mother Sallow's twine.
Her blade slips on the slick flesh and nicks the sac; it bursts in her hands.
Bile sprays her wrists and forearms, and the skin there stings like nettles.
The jar stays empty. In the gut beside it lies a brass-buckled belt with a bowman's knife.
Jory goes quiet, staring at the belt in her hand. "That's Dickon's."
He presses a gold coin into her stinging palm. "From both crews, like I said. You earned it."
Tam Hobb, stout and grey, eyes the head. "Eighty pound if it's an ounce. A long haul to town."
"Take my mill barrow. Send it back on any barge coming down; I mean to grind by afternoon."
